title: Florida House, District 63
what_it_does: Represents District 63 in the Florida House of Representatives; votes on state laws and the state budget.
decided_note: Jacqueline Coffie-Leeks is listed as Unopposed by the Florida Division of Elections after winning the Aug. 18, 2026 Democratic primary, so the seat is filled without a November vote. Sources: Florida Division of Elections candidate list (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp), checked Sept. 21, 2026.
verified_ballot_note: Tampa Bay Times (Aug. 18, 2026): 'HD 63 (Tampa) Democratic Primary: This open seat was won by Jacqueline Coffie-Leeks against Robin Lockett, and Conrad Schupay' (https://www.tampabay.com/news/florida-politics/elections/2026/08/18/florida-legislature-house-senate-legislative-results-primary-2026/). Florida Politics describes HD 63 as inland Hillsborough including Temple Terrace, Sulphur Springs, West Tampa and Ybor City. Research limitation: every WebFetch (Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, Division of Elections, county SOEs, news sites) was blocked and the search budget was capped, so this roster comes only from search-result snippets and should be re-verified against the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

housing.summary: In her 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, Coffie-Leeks listed making housing more attainable among the policies she is personally passionate about, alongside youth career pathways, support for seniors and caregivers, and neighborhood investment. She did not name specific housing programs or proposals.
housing.quote: Whether it's helping a young person find a career pathway, making housing more attainable, supporting seniors and caregivers, strengthening our workforce, or investing in neighborhoods, my focus is on ensuring every resident has an opportunity to succeed.
